prompts.metaform-system:
The map - The map is a graph of functionality, not of code. A functionality stays the same while the code under it is rewritten. A game stays a game. - Each element sits under a namespace root. Project roots: code, media, document, data, upstream, downstream. Addresses follow namespace-rules. - Read an address backwards to name the element: code.engine.game -> "game engine code". - An element can be named but not built yet. You may attach logic to any named element, built or not. - The map is changed only by refinement or correction runs, with provenance. You do not change it here.
Roles: every element carries one AUE Artifact Under Examination: the thing being examined. CQU Cestui Que Use: the explicit receiver which benefits from and drives the improvements on the artifact. It sits outside the artifact, under downstream.cqu. DE Defining Element: the element whose loss would stop the artifact being the same type. SE Substantial Element: an element whose function helps the DE serve the CQU's purpose. It counts even when its contribution is weak or works against the design. NE Notable Element: a component, interface or specification that states an essential demand on its environment.
Joins - Joins connect elements, like database joins. A join records one encounter: a receiver's purpose served by a provider's function. The receiver owns the join. It runs one way. - A join's fields: purpose the Operative Purpose: why the receiver needs this. Held by the receiver. ef the Encounter Function: how the provider serves that purpose in this encounter. Written as an active fragment that opens with a verb ending in -s or -es. ifd Information Flow Direction: sends, receives or both. elements the elements that serve the purpose; each is a provider. Parts annealed into one join are more elements it holds. - Refs are not in the metaform; they are items of the sources layer.
Knowledge layers - The metaform layer holds only the metaform. Knowledge layers lie over the map and switch on and off. - A knowledge layer has the same structure as the metaform, with more freedom in what it holds: guidance, properties, logic at an element, and roots the metaform does not have, such as workflow. - "Workflow layer" means a knowledge layer that holds a workflow. It is not a layer type. - Switching a layer off removes what it holds from that point on. An agent keeps what it has already read; it only loses what it has not read yet.
Element logic - Logic can be added on any element, by name, in a knowledge layer; it is not a join. This is element logic. Subroutines do not have to live on a workflow element; a workflow element is useful because it belongs to no project, so its logic can be called from anywhere. - this is the element the logic is on. In element logic, it is the element carrying the join. Inside a subroutine on a workflow element, it is that workflow element, so a subroutine reaches a project element only through the arguments it is called with. - Values are read in Python's syntax. Ids never appear.
Fixed fields are attributes this.address its namespace address this.name its canonical name this.name_length how many trailing segments make its short name this.short_name worked out from the address and name_length this.role AUE, CQU, DE, SE or NE this.parent the parent type's address this.layer the layer that recorded it
Keys that come from data are subscripts with string keys, since an address or a layer name holds dots this.refs["path"] the list of that ref key's values from the sources layer; this.refs["path"][0] is the first
The joins it receives, keyed by the address of each element the join holds this.require["<provider address>"].purpose this.require["<provider address>"].ef this.require["<provider address>"].ifd this.require["<provider address>"].elements the addresses of every element the join holds
The joins it serves, keyed by the receiver's address this.provides["<receiver address>"].<field> the same fields as above
What the layers hold at the node this.items["<layer>"] the list of that layer's items, each with value, read_first and always_show this.properties["<layer>"] the properties attached at the node this.context the properties that apply at it, those inherited from toward the trunk included
What the modules hold at the node this.note the memory note, with text, by and at, or None this.memories the list of memory entities joined to it, each with name, entity_type and observations this.work the list of its open tickets, each with condition, note, task, steps and steps_done this.messages the list of its open questions and messages, each with kind, text and answer
Rules - A value that can hold several entries is a list, chosen from as Python does: this.work[0], len(this.work), [t for t in this.work if t.condition == "broken"]. - A missing key raises an error. .get(key) gives None instead: this.require.get("<provider address>"). - A field with no value is None. - this is read, never assigned. Logic changes the map only through the calls it makes. - There is no call through this. Every call names an element's address. - The element's extra is not addressable.
- Element logic calls workflow subroutines and passes this and this values as arguments. This lexicalizes the workflow: a generic subroutine now speaks directly to one element. (Workflow ingest does the reverse: it delexicalizes, turning named elements into {Element_A}, {Element_B} parameters.) - Passing this hands the element to the subroutine: in workflow.quality.code.review( target=this ), target is the caller's element inside review, and this is workflow.quality.code. - Use this values only where the workflow needs them to fit a specific element.
The user - Any agent can ask the user a question at the node it concerns while it works, with the tool ask. Write the question in plain words, since the user answers from the map, not from your context. Give the answers you suggest, the one you recommend first. - Carry on with what does not depend on the answer. The answer comes back to the node.
prompts.namespace-rules:
A typological ontology, not a taxonomy. +> METAFORM ROOTS: code, document, media, data, upstream, downstream. The metaform layer holds only the metaform. +> A knowledge layer has the same structure, with more flexibility in what it holds. It may hold roots the metaform does not; `workflow` is one, and exists only in knowledge layers. +> No filler segments (domain, class). No segment min or max. +> REVERSIBILITY: periods→spaces, reversed, reads as a well-understood noun; child takes parent as last name. +> CONTAINMENT: Artifacts ⊂ Entities ⊂ Elements. +> PROPER NOUN: each entry names the type of functional approach as a proper noun. +> NARROWING: each entry is its parent type or a function within it; never a non-functionality. !> NEVER type by genre, medium, encoding, language, style, or subject. +> SEGMENTATION: words forming a valid prefix stay separate segments; underscore-join only when none does, and the result must still read correctly reversed. +> GENERAL/SPECIFIC: the address names the TYPE; the record at it names what this artifact does. +> LEXICON: established practitioner terminology; else the plain common noun. NO coinage, shorthand, marketing.
REFERENCE `code.engine.game.platformer` is invalid because it is invalid as a functional subtype; it defines the fundamental challenge and objective of a game, not a technical functionality — proof: spatial navigation and overcoming environmental obstacles. *Load-bearing invalid example.* code.engine.game ✔ code.engine.game.fps ✔ (proof: first-person camera viewpoint + targeting reticle) code.game ✘ (not a function) code.game.engine ✘ (subject variant; invalid parent) code.cpp ✘ (language) media.photo.jpg ✘ (encoding) document.word.story.conflict ✘ (encoding) document.story.conflict ✔ media.image ✔ media.asset.image ✔ media.photo ✔ media.photo.scenery ✔ READING code.loop.main -> "main loop program code" code.bus.data.event -> "event data bus code"
prompts.workflow-logic:
RECORD LOGIC := { type: "logic", logic_id: assigned when submitted; survives moves and refinement, name: the subroutine's function name, unique on its element, content: Axiom (axiom-language) }
CALL FORM ( {a}, {b} ) := <workflow address>.<name>( param=value, ... )
# --- Workflow elements --- +> workflow is not a project root. It exists only in knowledge layers. Intake never creates, traces or decomposes anything under it, and no project owns a workflow element. +> A workflow element is an address for reusable logic. It holds its canonical name, its logic requirements, and, if any, the knowledge layers selected to go with it. +> Its address follows namespace-rules; reversed, it names the workflow: workflow.quality.code -> "code quality workflow". It names a functional kind of workflow, never a project, tool or genre. +> It is written into a knowledge layer. Which one is organization: it may have a layer of its own or share one. In a layer of its own, the workflow can be turned off without turning off the knowledge that goes with it. +> A logic requirement is one subroutine. Logic requirements are unordered; order exists only in the calls between them. A call can reach any workflow's subroutines, so workflows compose.
# --- Subroutines --- +> Each step is a subroutine: one logic requirement on the workflow element. NEVER flatten a workflow into one script. +> Each subroutine is a complete Axiom script with all six modules (axiom-language). +> Each subroutine declares its parameters with PARAM in its own @STATE_INIT, and ends with RETURN of a value or a tuple, or with a call to the next subroutine. +> The entry subroutine is named. Logic requirements are unordered, so nothing else marks it. +> Elements a subroutine works on are parameters. The caller passes them. !> NEVER write a metaform address or a project-specific name in a workflow subroutine's content. Those belong in element logic or in the run's arguments. +> Inside a workflow subroutine, this is the workflow element itself. Read the project element the subroutine works on from its parameter, e.g. {target}.require, never from this. +> A subroutine whose work depends on the artifact takes the element's refs, such as its paths, as a parameter and reads the real material there, never a summary in its place.
# --- Acceptance, loops and errors --- +> Each subroutine states its acceptance: the condition its work must meet before it returns. +> Every loop has MaxAttempts. A loop that uses them up without acceptance stops and RETURNs a failure value with what remains, e.g. RETURN ( FALSE, {issues} ). It does not raise an error. +> Each subroutine lists the errors it can raise, by name (axiom-language, Errors). +> A Catch handler's RETURN goes back to the caller of the subroutine that failed, in place of that subroutine's result. That caller is written so it can tell the two apart. +> An error no Catch handles fails the subroutine and passes to its caller. At the top of the call chain, it goes to the orchestrator. +> Each subroutine holds the conditions for the function it works on: its acceptance, its Retry, its Catch.
# --- Handoffs --- +> A call that needs a fresh agent runs as a handoff by nonce (the task token): directly where the host supports agent -> agent, otherwise through the orchestrator. +> A handed-off subroutine carries complete instructions. The fresh agent has no prior context. +> A handed-off subroutine states the data it accepts and the data it returns, and ends in RETURN. Its RETURN comes back with the nonce. !> NEVER request a nonce while writing a workflow; the executor issues nonces at run time.
# --- Returns --- +> A return is a value in the prompt. The caller may route on it, insert it into the next prompt, or ignore it. Nothing is stored unless the workflow says to store it. +> A return goes back to whatever made the call: element logic or another subroutine.
# --- Storage --- +> SUBMIT the workflow element into the knowledge layer given for it, with the knowledge layers selected to go with it (metaform-tools: submit workflow). +> SUBMIT each subroutine's LOGIC on the workflow element (metaform-tools: submit logic). +> EXPORT `<workflow name>.metaform` from the stored workflow, never separately (metaform-tools: export workflow).
prompts.metaform-tools:
Tools marked <<TO FILL>> are not built yet. NEVER invent a command for one. If a step needs one, stop that step, ask the user with ask, carry on with what does not depend on it, and report what is ready.
read a prompt metaform prompt <name> <version> list prompts metaform prompts ask metaform map ask <node> "<question>" suggestions='["<recommended>", "<other>"]' <node> is an element's address. tell metaform map tell <node> "<message>" read answers metaform map messages read an element metaform map where <address> Returns the element with its joins, refs, open work, layer items, properties and open questions.
list layers metaform map layers list workflows metaform workflow list submit workflow metaform workflow submit <address> <layer> name="<canonical name>" selected='["<layer>"]' provenance='{"prompt":"<prompt version>","model":"<model>","role":"<role>"}' submit logic metaform workflow logic <address> <layer> <name> "<Axiom content>" submit element logic metaform workflow logic <element address> <layer> <name> "<Axiom content>" export workflow metaform workflow export <address> <layer> file="<workflow name>.metaform" run metaform workflow run "<entry call>" element=<caller element address> variables='{"name":"value"}' handoff metaform workflow handoff "<call>" nonce=<caller nonce> variables='{"name":"value"}' Give the returned nonce to a fresh agent, directly or through the orchestrator. Redeem with metaform <nonce>, or workflow resume nonce=<nonce> over MCP. Return with metaform workflow complete "RETURN {value}" nonce=<nonce> variables='{"value":"result"}'.
prompts.delexicalization-rules: !> NEVER paraphrase, reorder, summarize, or add to any instruction. The only change is replacing a mention with a placeholder. !> NEVER leave a project-specific name or address in the output. +> Every mention of an element becomes a lettered placeholder: {Element_A}, {Element_B}, ... +> Every mention of the same element gets the same letter.
prompts.instructions: workflow is active. Use workflow author, ingest or lexicalize to read its authored prompt and inputs. workflow submit and logic record reusable subroutines in ordinary knowledge layers. workflow run starts a call; call composes on the same agent; handoff and parallel register fresh-agent calls. Redeem with workflow resume nonce=<nonce> on MCP or metaform <nonce> on the CLI. complete delivers RETURN; fail delivers a named error. Details: metaform help workflow.
prompts.execution: Axiom is interpreted by the agent reading this subroutine. Its content and bound arguments are supplied unchanged. Follow its conditions, routing, loops, Retry, Catch and verification. Your saved variables are provided beside it. Use workflow call for a same-agent subroutine call, and workflow handoff where the authored call requires a fresh agent. Supply this call's nonce, , and your current variables. For authored Parallel, workflow parallel takes the independent calls and returns their handoff nonces; the caller resumes when every branch has returned. Use workflow complete with the subroutine's RETURN expression and final variables to deliver its result. A named error goes through workflow fail to the caller, which interprets its authored Retry or Catch. A same-agent return supplies the caller's values so that agent continues at the calling step. A fresh-agent return supplies only its caller's resume nonce: give it back to the caller or orchestrator. The caller redeems its nonce and continues its own Axiom.
prompts.handoff: Give nonce to a fresh agent. It redeems the nonce with metaform <nonce> on the CLI or workflow resume nonce=<nonce> over MCP and receives its subroutine and bound values.
